nitmiluk-national-park-1.name: Katherine Gorge

nitmiluk-national-park-2.name: Edith Falls

nitmiluk-national-park-3.name: Jatbula Trail

katherine-1.name: Katherine Museum

katherine-3.name: Cutta Cutta Caves Nature Park

destination.name: Nitmiluk National Park
destination.tagline: Sandstone gorges, plunge pools and a 62 km walk on Jawoyn country east of Katherine.
destination.description: Nitmiluk National Park is Jawoyn country, a chain of sandstone gorges cut by the Katherine River about 30 km from Katherine town. Visitors cruise or paddle the gorges, swim at Leliyn (Edith Falls) on the western side, or walk the Jatbula Trail between the two. The Nitmiluk Visitor Centre at the gorge is the first stop for cruises, canoe hire and helicopter flights.
whyVisit: Cruise Nitmiluk Gorge with Jawoyn guides
Paddle a canoe through the gorges
Swim below the falls at Leliyn

goodToKnow.title: Parks pass required
goodToKnow.detail: Visitors need an NT Parks Visitor Pass: $10 adult per day, $20 for three days. NT residents are exempt.

goodToKnow.title: Wet-season water levels
goodToKnow.detail: Rain from November to April lifts river levels and can restrict gorge activities; swimming at Leliyn may close from November to April.

goodToKnow.title: Book the Jatbula Trail
goodToKnow.detail: Numbers are limited and walking and camping fees are paid online when you book, so reserve well ahead of the dry season.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The dry season, {months}, is the time for gorge cruises, canoeing and the Jatbula Trail; from November to April rising water can restrict activities.

Whether the NT Parks pass is $10 and Leliyn Nov-Apr restriction from Tourism NT pages. Free-text 'Jawoyn' (Nitmiluk Tours is Jawoyn-owned; Leliyn tourism page and cruise 'Jawoyn guides').

destination.name: Katherine
destination.tagline: The Top End's southern hub on the Katherine River, gateway to Nitmiluk and the Savannah Way.
destination.description: Katherine is the Northern Territory's third-largest town, sitting on the Stuart Highway and the Katherine River. It is the regional base for Nitmiluk Gorge 30 km to the north-east and for the Mataranka thermal pools to the south. In town, the museum and School of the Air tell the story of life in the outback, and Cutta Cutta Caves lie 27 km down the highway.
whyVisit: Tour the limestone chambers of Cutta Cutta Caves
See School of the Air lessons at work

goodToKnow.title: Cave tours need shoes
goodToKnow.detail: Cutta Cutta tours run April to October and require fully enclosed shoes; thongs and sandals are turned away.

goodToKnow.title: Plan around weekdays
goodToKnow.detail: Most shops close on weekends and School of the Air tours run on school-term weekdays, so schedule town stops early in the week.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The dry season, {months}, is the time to visit: Cutta Cutta tours run, gorge swimming and canoeing are open and the days are mild.

destinations.notes: Pin = OSM place=town 'Katherine' (Photon), 3 km from the Museum and 1.5 km from School of the Air. Recommended importance order: katherine-3 (Cutta Cutta Caves), katherine-1 (Museum), katherine-2 (School of the Air) - ids unchanged. Only 3 spots; hub rule applies (owner may prefer standalone). 'Third-largest town' and ~10,000 from placement; shops-close-weekends from Wikivoyage; School of the Air weekday term tours from a guide listing (unverified).
